newsitem.title: UK: Israeli president makes first state visit to UK.
newsitem.headline: Israeli president makes first state visit to UK.

text.p: Ezer Weizman, a former fighter pilot turned combatant for Middle East peace, on Tuesday begins the first state visit by an Israeli president to Britain.

Invited by Queen Elizabeth, Weizman and his London-born wife Reuma will mix banquets and memorials on a trip that takes them from the palaces of London to the learned libraries of Cambridge and a key air force base in Lincolnshire.

"The queen and (her husband Philip) the Duke of Edinburgh are looking forward very much to the state visit and see it as an expression of warmth in our relationship at the very highest level," said a Buckingham Palace spokesman.
"It's the first state visit by an Israeli president and the queen herself has not yet visited the state of Israel."

Should Weizman -- whose five-year term ends in May 1998 -- return the queen's invitation, it would be up to government ministers to decide if she accepted and embarked on a trip rich with symbolism as Israel prepares for its 50th year as an independent state.
"We will wait and see," said the palace spokesman.
For his part, Weizman wants his landmark visit to stress Israel's place in the new world order.

"Israel is striving always towards better relations with Western countries, and this visit will increase friendly relations and discuss in very general terms trade and economic development," said an Israeli embassy spokeswoman.
The state of Israel was created in 1948 out of British-controlled Palestine. Palestine, for long inhabited mainly by Arabs, was part of the Ottoman Empire until captured by the British in 1917-18.

The visit comes amid heightened tensions in the peace process, with many Arab countries fearful for progress following the election of hardline Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. But the spokeswoman said relations with the West were now better than at many times in the past, hence the go-ahead for a visit.

"Israel has had its ups and downs and it is only in the last few years the relationship has been so good. We want to show we're willing to discuss anything with anybody -- new friends, old friends, enemies who have become new friends. We want to move into the Western world," she said.
A British official said Weizman had long championed the cause of peace, noting that his visit was finalised after Netanyahu's election.
"This is a brave and imaginative fighter for peace. This is a man who has links with both sides and whose contribution should be applauded," he said.
"He has at least a strong indirect influence on the way in which the peace process is conducted."

The Weizmans will be accorded a full ceremonial arrival with a carriage procession to Buckingham Palace. Lunch with members of the royal family will be "very informal and very jolly", followed by meetings with members of the Jewish community, tea with the Queen Mother and a state banquet on Tuesday night.
On Wednesday, Weizman will hold talks with Prime Minister John Major and leaders of opposition parties, before visiting the Bank of England and Rothschild and Sons Ltd in London's financial district.
Queen Elizabeth will unveil a monument to Raoul Wallenberg, the Swedish diplomat who saved thousands of Jews from extermination by the Nazis, and Weizman will attend a synagogue.
On his final day, the president meets United Nations Secretary General Kofi Annan and visits a Cambridge University library to inspect manuscripts dating back to the ninth century.
The former Royal Air Force pilot will also visit a RAF base at Cranwell and contribute to a Holocaust exhibit in London.

The visit will awaken old memories for Weizman, whose wife was born in London, whose uncle -- the first president of Israel -- spent time in Manchester and who himself served in Britain's RAF during World War Two, flying in India, Egypt and beyond.
